roles.title: Senior QA Engineer
roles.overview: A Senior QA Engineer is an experienced individual contributor who owns quality for complex features or an entire product area. They lead by example rather than by managing people: shaping test approaches, mentoring others, influencing design decisions early and handling the hardest testing problems.
responsibilities: Own the test approach for complex features from requirements review to release
Identify product and technical risks early in refinement and design discussions
Design and review test cases, automation and test data written by others
Mentor junior and mid-level testers through pairing and feedback
Investigate difficult defects across front end, API and database layers
Improve team practices such as defect triage, automation reliability or test data management
Communicate quality status and residual risk clearly to the team

essential: Advanced test design techniques and risk-based testing
Automation competence in at least one stack
roleSpecific: Mentoring and constructive code and test review
Influencing without authority
Root cause analysis across system layers
optional: A domain specialisation such as payments or healthcare

prerequisites: Several years of hands-on testing experience
Working automation and API testing skills

beginner.title: Owning a feature's quality
goals: Write a risk-based test approach for a feature and review it with the developers
Raise testability and ambiguity issues during refinement before development starts
Debug a defect down to the failing layer and propose the likely cause
Review a colleague's test cases with specific, actionable feedback

intermediate.title: Raising the team's level
goals: Mentor a junior tester through a full feature cycle
Lead a defect triage session and settle severity disagreements with evidence
Reduce flaky tests or slow suites in a measurable way
Define exploratory charters for a high-risk release

advanced.title: Technical quality leadership
goals: Propose and drive a practice change across the team with a measured outcome
Contribute to test architecture decisions for a new service
Present residual risk and a release recommendation to stakeholders
Act as backup for the QA lead on planning and coordination

exercises: Write a one-page risk-based test approach for a password reset redesign
Review a pull request of automation code and give five prioritised comments
Prepare a 15-minute mentoring session on writing defect reports
Analyse three months of escaped defects and propose one process change

sampleProject.title: Quality improvement case study
sampleProject.description: On a project you work on or a realistic demo app, identify one quality problem (such as flaky UI tests or late defect discovery), measure the baseline, introduce a change (stabilised waits, earlier requirement reviews or API-level tests), and document the before-and-after measurements, trade-offs and what you would do next.

interviewQuestions.q: Tell me about a time you found a significant risk early. What did you do?
interviewQuestions.a: A strong answer follows situation, task, action and result: for example, noticing during refinement that a refund feature had no defined behaviour for partial refunds after currency conversion, raising it with concrete examples, getting the product owner to decide the rule before coding, and adding decision-table tests. The result is described honestly, including what was learned.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you mentor a junior tester who writes vague defect reports?
interviewQuestions.a: I pair on a few defects, showing what a developer needs: clear steps, environment, expected versus actual, evidence and impact. I give a simple checklist, review their next reports with specific feedback and recognise improvement. I focus on why each element helps reproduction and prioritisation rather than imposing a template.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you handle a developer who disagrees that something is a defect?
interviewQuestions.a: I return to the requirement, acceptance criteria or user impact, show evidence, and ask what they understand the expected behaviour to be. If it is genuinely ambiguous, it becomes a product decision, so I bring in the product owner. The goal is the right outcome for users, not winning the argument.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you decide what not to test?
interviewQuestions.a: Using risk: likelihood of failure and impact if it fails, informed by change scope, complexity, past defects and usage. Low-risk, stable areas get lighter coverage or rely on existing automation. I make the decision explicit and communicate the residual risk rather than silently skipping.

interviewQuestions.q: What separates a senior QA engineer from a mid-level one?
interviewQuestions.a: Scope and influence: a senior engineer handles ambiguous problems independently, sees risk across features and layers, improves how the whole team works, mentors others and communicates trade-offs to stakeholders, while still doing hands-on testing.

roles.codingRequirements: Expected to write and review automation code competently in the team's stack. The depth varies by company, but a senior QA engineer should be able to debug tests and read application code.
commonMistakes: Doing all the hard testing alone instead of growing others
Reporting only test counts rather than risk and impact
Joining a feature only after development, missing the chance to prevent defects
Pushing personal preferences in reviews without explaining reasons
readinessCriteria: Has owned the test approach for at least one complex feature end to end
Has mentored at least one colleague with visible improvement
Can explain a release recommendation in terms of residual risk
Has led a measurable practice improvement

roles.title: QA Lead
roles.overview: A QA Lead coordinates quality work for a team or product so that testing is planned, prioritised and delivered on time. They still do hands-on testing in many organisations, but their main value is in planning, assigning and unblocking work, keeping quality visible and being the quality voice in day-to-day delivery decisions.
responsibilities: Plan testing activities for sprints and releases and align them with the delivery plan
Assign and balance testing work across the QA team members
Run or facilitate defect triage and track critical defects to resolution
Agree entry and exit criteria and quality gates with the product and engineering leads
Report test progress, defect status and risks to stakeholders
Coach team members and support their day-to-day development
Identify process bottlenecks such as environment instability and drive fixes

roleSpecific: Coordinating work across testers and squads
Facilitating triage and resolving priority conflicts
Agile delivery practices and ceremonies

prerequisites: Experience as a senior or experienced tester

beginner.title: Planning and coordination
goals: Write a release test plan with scope, approach, schedule and risks
Estimate testing effort for a release and explain assumptions
Run a daily defect triage with clear outcomes
Produce a concise weekly quality status report

intermediate.title: Leading delivery quality
goals: Define and apply entry and exit criteria for a release
Rebalance team work when priorities change mid-sprint
Run a retrospective focused on escaped defects
Make a release recommendation with residual risk

advanced.title: Improving team effectiveness
goals: Introduce a quality metric that drives a decision and retire one that does not
Plan the balance of manual, exploratory and automated testing for the team
Grow a team member into a senior role
Coordinate testing across multiple dependent teams for a release

exercises: Write a test plan for a three-sprint release of a checkout redesign
Given 40 open defects and two days to release, run a mock triage and decide what blocks release
Design a one-page weekly status report that a product manager can read in two minutes
Plan work allocation for three testers with different skills across five stories

sampleProject.title: Release quality pack
sampleProject.description: For a realistic release scenario, produce a test plan, an estimation with assumptions, entry and exit criteria, a risk register, a triage log for a sample defect list and a final release recommendation explaining residual risks. Present it as a short document a delivery team could use.

interviewQuestions.q: The release date is fixed and testing is behind. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.a: I make the situation visible early with facts: what is tested, what is not and the associated risk. Then I re-prioritise remaining testing by risk, look for ways to add capacity such as developer help or focusing automation, and propose options to stakeholders: release with documented residual risk, reduce scope, or move the date. The decision belongs to the business owner, but it must be informed.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you run an effective defect triage?
interviewQuestions.a: With the right people (product, development and QA), a prepared list, and a time box. For each defect we confirm reproducibility, agree severity and priority, assign an owner and a target, and mark duplicates or rejects with reasons. Outcomes are recorded so decisions are traceable.

interviewQuestions.q: Tell me about a conflict in your team and how you resolved it.
interviewQuestions.a: A strong answer describes a real situation, such as two testers disagreeing about test ownership, how the lead listened to both, clarified the goal and responsibilities, agreed a working arrangement, followed up and what changed. It shows fairness and a focus on outcomes rather than blame.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you decide what goes in a quality status report?
interviewQuestions.a: I ask what decisions the readers need to make. Typically: progress against plan, open critical defects and their trend, risks and blockers with owners, and a clear statement of readiness. Raw counts without context get removed.

interviewQuestions.q: How much hands-on testing should a QA lead do?
interviewQuestions.a: It depends on team size. In a small team, a lead tests regularly and stays close to the product. As the team grows, coordination, coaching and stakeholder work take more time, but some hands-on work keeps judgement grounded. I would not hold the critical path alone, because lead duties interrupt testing.

roles.codingRequirements: Coding depth depends on the team. Leads of automation-heavy teams are expected to review automation code; others focus on planning and coordination. Reading CI results and basic SQL is broadly useful.
commonMistakes: Becoming the bottleneck by testing the critical path personally
Reporting optimistic status and surprising stakeholders late
Treating every defect as a release blocker without risk-based prioritisation
Neglecting team members' development under delivery pressure
readinessCriteria: Has written a release test plan with estimates and risks
Has run defect triage and made release recommendations
Can describe a conflict or priority clash they resolved
Can present quality status that leads to decisions

roles.title: Test Lead
roles.overview: A Test Lead leads the testing effort for a project, programme or test phase, often in structured or contract-based delivery where formal test planning and reporting are expected. They define the test approach for their scope, coordinate test execution across testers and sometimes vendors, and report against agreed criteria. The title overlaps heavily with QA Lead; Test Lead tends to emphasise test-phase delivery while QA Lead often implies broader process quality.
responsibilities: Write the test plan for a project or test phase from the organisational test strategy
Plan test phases such as system, integration and user acceptance testing and their dependencies
Coordinate test environments, test data and access with other teams
Lead daily test execution, track progress and manage defects
Maintain traceability between requirements, tests and defects
Produce test progress and test completion reports
Support user acceptance testing with business users

roleSpecific: Coordinating test environments and data across teams
Managing UAT with business stakeholders
Working with test vendors or distributed teams
optional: ISTQB Advanced Test Manager or similar certification
Domain knowledge such as finance or public sector

prerequisites: Experience as a test analyst or tester on structured projects
Understanding of test levels and test documentation

beginner.title: Test phase planning
goals: Write a phase test plan including scope, approach, environments, entry and exit criteria
Build a traceability matrix from requirements to tests
Plan test data and environment needs with lead times
Report daily execution progress against plan

intermediate.title: Running test execution
goals: Coordinate system integration testing across two dependent teams
Plan and support a UAT cycle with business users
Manage defect flow and escalation for blocking issues
Write a test completion report with recommendation

advanced.title: Leading complex test programmes
goals: Estimate and schedule multiple test phases with dependencies
Manage test risk and issue logs at programme level
Coordinate vendor or offshore testers with clear deliverables
Contribute to organisational test strategy

exercises: Write a system integration test plan for a payment service integrating with a bank gateway simulator
Build a traceability matrix for 15 requirements and identify coverage gaps
Prepare a UAT kick-off agenda and briefing for business users
Write a test completion report from a provided set of execution and defect data

sampleProject.title: Test phase documentation set
sampleProject.description: For a realistic system integration scenario, produce a phase test plan, environment and data plan, traceability matrix, daily progress report template and a test completion report with an exit recommendation, using sample execution data you generate and label as illustrative.

interviewQuestions.q: What goes into a test plan for a test phase?
interviewQuestions.a: Scope and out-of-scope items, test approach and techniques, test items and features, entry and exit criteria, environments and test data, schedule and dependencies, roles and responsibilities, risks with mitigations, deliverables and how progress will be reported. It should derive from the organisation's test strategy and be specific enough to act on.

interviewQuestions.q: Exit criteria say no open high-severity defects, but two remain and the business wants to go live. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.a: I present the facts: what the two defects are, their impact, workarounds and fix timelines. Exit criteria inform the decision but the business owner decides whether to accept the risk. If they accept, I make sure the acceptance is documented with owners and dates for the fixes, and that support teams know about the workarounds.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you prepare business users for UAT?
interviewQuestions.a: Agree the scope and acceptance criteria with them, provide scenarios based on their real processes, set up environments and data in advance, give a short briefing on how to log issues, and provide daily support. UAT checks fitness for business use, so I avoid turning it into a repeat of system testing.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you handle a test environment that is constantly unavailable?
interviewQuestions.a: Log the downtime and its impact on the schedule so the problem is visible with facts, escalate to the environment owner with that data, agree a booking or support arrangement, and replan around it by prioritising tests that can run elsewhere, for example API tests against mocks.

interviewQuestions.q: Describe how you use a traceability matrix.
interviewQuestions.a: It links requirements to tests and to defects. I use it to find requirements without tests, to assess impact when a requirement changes, and to report coverage and outcomes per requirement in the completion report. It needs to be maintained during the project, not created at the end.

roles.codingRequirements: Coding is usually not required for a Test Lead, though understanding automation and being able to read test reports from CI is valuable. Spreadsheet and reporting skills are used heavily.
commonMistakes: Writing a generic test plan copied from another project
Underestimating environment and test data lead times
Treating UAT as a second round of system testing
Creating traceability at the end instead of maintaining it
readinessCriteria: Has written a phase test plan with entry and exit criteria
Can build and use a traceability matrix to find coverage gaps
Has coordinated or supported a UAT cycle
Can produce a test completion report with a recommendation

roles.title: Test Manager
roles.overview: A Test Manager is accountable for testing across multiple projects or a test function, including the people, process and budget involved. They set test strategy within their scope, staff and develop the test team, manage test vendors and environments, and represent testing at programme and management level.
responsibilities: Define and maintain test strategy and policy for the projects or function they own
Hire, line-manage and develop testers and test leads
Plan testing budgets, resourcing and tool investments
Manage relationships with test vendors and outsourced teams
Oversee test planning, progress and reporting across projects
Manage test risks and escalate them at programme level
Drive test process improvement using measured outcomes

essential: Test strategy and test management practices
People management: hiring, performance and development
roleSpecific: Vendor and contract management for testing services
Test process assessment and improvement
Programme-level risk management
optional: ISTQB Advanced Test Manager or similar

prerequisites: Experience as a test lead or QA lead

beginner.title: From lead to manager
goals: Write a test strategy covering several projects with shared standards
Run regular one-to-ones and set development goals with team members
Build a resource plan for the next quarter across projects
Report testing status across projects in one consistent format

intermediate.title: Managing the test function
goals: Build a business case for a test tool or automation investment with honest costs and benefits
Hire for a role using a structured interview process
Set up a vendor engagement with clear deliverables and quality measures
Run a process improvement with before-and-after measurements

advanced.title: Strategic test management
goals: Align test strategy with organisational delivery and risk priorities
Plan capability development such as automation or performance skills across the team
Handle underperformance fairly and constructively
Represent testing in governance and release boards

exercises: Write a test strategy for an organisation running three projects of different risk levels
Draft a business case for an automation investment, listing costs, assumptions and how benefits will be measured
Design a structured interview plan for a mid-level tester
Prepare a one-to-one plan for a tester who wants to move into automation

sampleProject.title: Test function plan
sampleProject.description: For a fictional organisation with clearly invented details, produce a test strategy, a team structure and hiring plan, a quarterly resource and budget plan with stated assumptions, a vendor engagement outline and a set of quality metrics with the decisions each metric supports.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you build the business case for test automation?
interviewQuestions.a: Start with the problem, such as long regression cycles delaying releases. Estimate costs honestly: tools, framework build, maintenance, training and the time before benefits appear. Estimate benefits as measurable changes, such as regression time, release frequency or escaped defects, with assumptions stated. Propose a pilot with success criteria rather than a large up-front commitment.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you handle a tester who is consistently underperforming?
interviewQuestions.a: First understand the cause through a private conversation: unclear expectations, skills gaps, workload or personal issues. Set clear, specific expectations, provide support such as training or pairing, agree a timeline and check in regularly with documented feedback. If there is no improvement despite support, follow the organisation's formal process fairly.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you decide between in-house testers and a testing vendor?
interviewQuestions.a: Consider the work's nature: long-term product knowledge and fast feedback favour in-house; peak capacity, specialist skills or well-defined repeatable work can suit a vendor. I weigh communication overhead, knowledge retention, contract flexibility and quality control, and define measurable deliverables in any vendor engagement.

interviewQuestions.q: What metrics would you report to senior management about testing?
interviewQuestions.a: Metrics tied to outcomes and decisions: escaped defects by severity, release readiness against criteria, test cycle time, automation stability and coverage of high-risk areas. I avoid vanity metrics like raw test case counts, and always provide context and trends rather than isolated numbers.

interviewQuestions.q: Tell me about a time you had to push back on a release decision.
interviewQuestions.a: A strong answer explains the risk evidence presented, the stakeholders involved, the options offered, the decision taken (which may have been to release with mitigations) and the outcome, showing that the manager informs decisions with data rather than acting as a gatekeeper.

roles.codingRequirements: Coding is not usually required. Understanding automation, CI and technical risks well enough to make sound investment and staffing decisions is expected.
commonMistakes: Measuring testers by test case or defect counts, which encourages the wrong behaviour
Promising automation savings without accounting for maintenance
Acting as the sole release gatekeeper instead of informing business decisions
Neglecting people development under delivery pressure
readinessCriteria: Has written a multi-project test strategy
Has line-managed or formally mentored testers with documented development goals
Can build a resource and budget plan with stated assumptions
Can explain how they would handle underperformance and vendor management

roles.title: QA Manager
roles.overview: A QA Manager leads a quality assurance team and owns quality processes for a product or department, covering people, process and budget. Compared with a Test Manager, the role usually places more weight on preventive quality practices, process standards and continuous delivery, rather than only managing test execution.
responsibilities: Hire, line-manage and develop QA engineers and leads
Define quality processes and standards such as definition of done, review practices and release criteria
Own the QA budget, tooling and headcount planning
Align QA priorities with product and engineering leadership
Embed QA engineers effectively in cross-functional teams
Track quality outcomes and lead improvement initiatives
Handle escalations about quality issues and customer-impacting defects

essential: Quality process design for agile delivery
roleSpecific: Designing team structures for embedded QA
Quality metrics and continuous improvement
Incident and escaped-defect review processes

prerequisites: Experience as a QA lead or test manager

beginner.title: Leading a QA team
goals: Set clear role expectations and career levels for QA engineers
Run one-to-ones and give regular feedback
Agree a definition of done that includes quality activities with engineering leads
Report quality outcomes monthly to product and engineering leadership

intermediate.title: Quality processes
goals: Introduce an escaped-defect review with action tracking
Plan headcount and tooling budget for the next year with assumptions
Balance embedded QA engineers with shared quality practices
Improve release readiness criteria with measurable gates

advanced.title: Department-level quality
goals: Define a quality roadmap aligned with product goals
Develop QA leads as future managers
Lead quality through organisational change such as a move to continuous delivery
Represent quality in executive discussions using outcome metrics

exercises: Write a career framework for QA engineers at three levels with observable behaviours
Design an escaped-defect review process with roles, cadence and outputs
Plan a year's QA budget with headcount, tools and training, listing assumptions
Prepare a monthly quality report for leadership using three outcome metrics

sampleProject.title: QA operating model
sampleProject.description: For a fictional product organisation with clearly invented details, document a QA operating model: team structure and embedding approach, career levels, quality processes (definition of done, release criteria, escaped-defect reviews), a metrics set with the decision each metric informs, and a 12-month improvement roadmap.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you structure QA in an organisation with eight product teams?
interviewQuestions.a: Usually by embedding QA engineers in teams so quality work happens alongside development, with a QA chapter or practice that shares standards, tools and learning. The ratio depends on risk, automation maturity and how much testing developers own. I would revisit the structure as teams mature rather than fixing a ratio permanently.

interviewQuestions.q: Customers report a severe bug that QA missed. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.a: First support the fix and customer communication. Then run a blameless review: how the defect was introduced, why reviews and tests did not catch it, and which change would prevent similar escapes, such as a missing test type, unclear requirement or environment gap. Actions get owners and dates. The aim is system improvement, not finding someone to blame.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you justify QA headcount to leadership?
interviewQuestions.a: By linking it to outcomes and risks they care about: release frequency, escaped defects, customer-impacting incidents and engineering time spent on rework, with honest assumptions. I also show the alternatives, such as investing in automation or shifting testing work into development teams, and their trade-offs.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you develop a QA engineer who wants to become a lead?
interviewQuestions.a: Agree the skills involved, then give progressively bigger opportunities: running triage, planning a release, mentoring a new hire. I give regular feedback and visibility with stakeholders, and make sure they also have the support to succeed rather than just extra work.

interviewQuestions.q: What is the difference between quality assurance and testing in your view?
interviewQuestions.a: Testing evaluates the product to find defects and provide information. Quality assurance is broader: the processes that prevent defects and give confidence that quality requirements will be met, such as requirement reviews, coding standards, definition of done and improvement loops. A QA manager owns both but should push effort toward prevention.

roles.codingRequirements: Coding is not normally required. Enough technical understanding to evaluate automation strategy, CI pipelines and engineering trade-offs is expected.
commonMistakes: Positioning QA as the only team responsible for quality
Using metrics such as defect counts per tester to compare individuals
Hiring before clarifying what the team needs QA engineers to do
Treating every escaped defect as an individual's failure
readinessCriteria: Has led a team with responsibility for hiring or development decisions
Can design quality processes for agile teams with measurable outcomes
Has planned a budget or headcount request with assumptions
Can describe running a blameless escaped-defect review

roles.title: Quality Engineering Manager
roles.overview: A Quality Engineering Manager owns quality strategy across engineering, treating quality as an engineering discipline rather than a separate testing phase. They lead quality engineers and SDETs, invest in test infrastructure and developer-owned testing, and use delivery and reliability data to decide where quality effort will have the most impact.
responsibilities: Define the engineering-wide quality strategy, including test layering, ownership and tooling
Lead and grow quality engineers, SDETs and test infrastructure engineers
Invest in shared test platforms, environments and CI capabilities
Enable developers to own testing through frameworks, guidance and coaching
Partner with engineering and SRE leadership on reliability, incidents and release practices
Use delivery metrics and escaped-defect data to target improvements
Make build-versus-buy decisions for quality tooling

essential: Test architecture and strategy across services and platforms
Engineering management: hiring, coaching and performance
roleSpecific: Developer enablement and influencing engineering culture
Test platform and infrastructure investment decisions
Reliability practices such as service level objectives and incident reviews
optional: Performance, security or chaos engineering background
Budget ownership for tooling and cloud costs

prerequisites: Strong technical background in automation or software engineering

beginner.title: Quality engineering foundations
goals: Assess current test layering and identify the biggest feedback-time or reliability gap
Agree testing ownership between developers and quality engineers
Establish a flaky-test and pipeline-health process
Set up regular one-to-ones and growth plans for the team

intermediate.title: Platforms and enablement
goals: Deliver a shared test framework or environment capability with adoption measured
Introduce contract testing or other techniques that reduce reliance on end-to-end tests
Partner with SRE on incident reviews and resulting test improvements
Make a documented build-versus-buy decision for a quality tool

advanced.title: Engineering-wide quality strategy
goals: Publish a quality strategy with measurable goals aligned to business priorities
Integrate non-functional quality (performance, security, resilience) into delivery
Report quality outcomes to engineering leadership with clear trade-offs
Grow quality engineering leaders

tools: Contract testing tools such as Pact
exercises: Assess a described system and propose a test layering strategy with ownership per layer
Write a build-versus-buy analysis for a visual regression tool
Design a quarterly plan to cut pipeline feedback time with measurable milestones
Map three recent incidents to test or process changes that would have prevented or detected them

sampleProject.title: Quality engineering strategy document
sampleProject.description: For a fictional microservice-based product with clearly invented details, write a quality engineering strategy: current-state assessment, target test layering and ownership, platform investments, non-functional quality integration, metrics with targets and decision rules, team structure and a phased roadmap with trade-offs stated.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you move an organisation from a separate QA phase to developer-owned quality?
interviewQuestions.a: Make it easier to do the right thing: provide frameworks, fast reliable pipelines and examples, pair quality engineers with developers, include testing in the definition of done and code review, and measure outcomes such as escaped defects and lead time. Quality engineers shift from executing tests to enabling, coaching and building infrastructure. It is a gradual change, started with willing teams.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you decide where to invest quality engineering effort?
interviewQuestions.a: Use data: escaped defects and incidents by area, pipeline duration and flakiness, change frequency and business criticality. I prioritise investments that reduce the largest risks or delays, estimate effort and expected impact, and review the outcomes after delivery.

interviewQuestions.q: When would you build an internal test tool rather than buy one?
interviewQuestions.a: Build when needs are specific to the organisation, no product fits, and the team can afford to maintain it long term. Buy or adopt open source when a mature tool meets most needs, since maintenance cost is often underestimated. I write down the total cost, the lock-in and exit options, and who will own it.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you work with SRE or operations teams on quality?
interviewQuestions.a: Share data from incidents and testing, join incident reviews to identify test gaps, align on reliability goals such as service level objectives, and collaborate on practices like canary releases, game days and production monitoring that complement pre-release testing.

interviewQuestions.q: Tell me about a strategy you introduced that did not work as planned.
interviewQuestions.a: A strong answer describes the decision and the assumptions behind it, what signals showed it was not working, how they adjusted or reversed it, and what they learned, showing comfort with evidence-based course correction rather than defending a plan.

roles.codingRequirements: A strong technical background is expected: able to review test architecture and framework code, understand CI/CD and system design, and make credible technical decisions. Day-to-day coding varies by organisation size.
commonMistakes: Building a large central automation suite that developers do not own or trust
Measuring success by number of automated tests instead of outcomes
Building internal tools without planning for long-term maintenance
Ignoring non-functional quality until late in delivery
readinessCriteria: Has led a technical quality initiative across multiple teams with measured results
Can design a test layering strategy for a distributed system with ownership
Has managed or mentored engineers
Can make and document a build-versus-buy decision

roles.title: Test Strategy Consultant
roles.overview: A Test Strategy Consultant advises organisations on how to test and assure quality, usually as an external or internal advisor rather than a delivery manager. They assess current practices, identify risks and gaps, recommend a target strategy and roadmap, and help teams adopt it, with success depending on credibility, evidence and communication.
responsibilities: Run test process and maturity assessments through interviews, artefact reviews and observation
Identify gaps and risks in current testing practices with supporting evidence
Recommend test strategies, operating models and tooling suited to the client's context
Build phased improvement roadmaps with priorities and measurable outcomes
Present findings and recommendations to technical and executive audiences
Coach teams and leaders during adoption
Define the scope of engagements and manage expectations

essential: Broad testing knowledge across levels, types and techniques
roleSpecific: Test process improvement and maturity models
Adapting strategy to different delivery models and regulatory contexts
Change management and stakeholder influence
optional: ISTQB Advanced or Expert level certifications
Domain expertise in a regulated industry
Specialist depth in automation, performance or security

prerequisites: Substantial experience leading testing or quality engineering
Exposure to several organisations, teams or delivery models

beginner.title: Assessment skills
goals: Prepare an assessment plan with interview questions and artefacts to review
Map a team's current test process and identify bottlenecks
Write findings backed by evidence rather than opinion
Distinguish symptoms from root causes in quality problems

intermediate.title: Recommendations and roadmaps
goals: Write a target test strategy tailored to context, including what not to change
Prioritise recommendations by impact, effort and dependency
Define measurable outcomes for each roadmap phase
Present findings to senior stakeholders and handle challenge

advanced.title: Advisory leadership
goals: Lead a multi-team assessment and roadmap engagement
Coach client leaders through adoption and adjust based on results
Advise on strategy for specialist areas such as AI systems, data or regulated releases
Define engagement scope, deliverables and success measures with clients

tools: Test management and tracker tools for review
exercises: Write an interview guide for assessing a team's test practice covering planning, design, automation, environments and reporting
Given a described organisation, write five findings with evidence, impact and recommendation
Build a phased 6-month improvement roadmap with outcomes and dependencies
Prepare a 10-minute executive summary presentation of an assessment

sampleProject.title: Test practice assessment report
sampleProject.description: For a fictional organisation with clearly invented details, produce a complete assessment: scope and method, current-state summary, evidence-backed findings, risks, a tailored target test strategy, a prioritised roadmap with measurable outcomes and an executive summary. State assumptions and limits of the assessment.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you run a test process assessment?
interviewQuestions.a: Agree scope and goals with the sponsor, then gather evidence from several sources: interviews across roles, reviews of plans, test cases, defect data and pipelines, and observation of real ceremonies. I compare against the organisation's goals rather than a one-size-fits-all ideal, validate findings with the people involved, and present evidence-backed findings with prioritised recommendations.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you avoid giving generic recommendations?
interviewQuestions.a: By tying every recommendation to a specific finding, its evidence and the client's goals and constraints, such as regulation, team skills and release model. I also say what should stay the same and why, and size recommendations to what the organisation can absorb.

interviewQuestions.q: A senior stakeholder strongly disagrees with your findings. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.a: Listen to understand their perspective and any evidence I might have missed, walk through the evidence behind the finding, and separate facts from interpretation. If they bring new information I update the finding; if not, I keep it, possibly reframed, and record the disagreement. Credibility depends on being evidence-led, not on agreement.

interviewQuestions.q: What would you recommend to a team that wants to 'automate everything'?
interviewQuestions.a: I would ask what problem they are trying to solve, such as slow regression or escaped defects, then recommend automation where it gives fast, reliable, valuable feedback, mostly at unit, API and contract levels, with a small set of end-to-end tests, while keeping exploratory testing for discovery. I would also plan for maintenance and skills.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you measure whether your recommendations worked?
interviewQuestions.a: Agree outcome measures and baselines at the start, such as release cycle time, escaped defects by severity or pipeline duration, then review them after each roadmap phase. I also gather qualitative feedback from teams, because adoption problems often show there first.

roles.codingRequirements: Coding is not required day to day, but enough technical depth to evaluate automation, CI/CD and architecture credibly is expected. Many consultants have a hands-on engineering or automation background.
commonMistakes: Applying a favourite framework or maturity model without adapting it to context
Making findings without evidence, which undermines credibility
Delivering a report and leaving without supporting adoption
Recommending too many changes at once
readinessCriteria: Has conducted or co-led a test practice assessment with written findings
Can produce a context-specific test strategy and phased roadmap
Has presented recommendations to senior stakeholders and handled challenge
Can explain how recommendation outcomes will be measured
